reports.title: Encuesta Permanente de Hogares Continua (EPHC)
reports.description: Continuous household survey that is the primary source for labour-market indicators, household income, and income-based poverty and inequality measurement. National coverage with urban/rural and departmental domains.
reports._notes: Central social and labour survey. Official source for both labour statistics and monetary poverty. Annual poverty results and quarterly labour bulletins are the main public products.

reports.title: Pobreza monetaria / Monetary poverty
reports.description: Official income-poverty and extreme-poverty incidence, calculated by comparing household per-capita income (from EPHC) with nationally defined poverty lines updated by the IPC. Published with urban/rural and departmental breakdowns.
reports._notes: Headline social indicator. 2024: total monetary poverty 20.1% (down 2.2 pp from 22.3% in 2023); extreme poverty 4.1%. Large urban–rural gap, especially in extreme poverty (rural much higher).

reports.title: Líneas de pobreza total y extrema
reports.description: Monetary values of the total and extreme poverty lines (per capita), differentiated for urban and rural areas and updated with the IPC produced by the Banco Central.
reports._notes: Direct input into the poverty measurement. Basket structures derived from income-and-expenditure surveys; annual updating uses the BCP IPC.

reports.title: Índice de Precios al Consumidor (IPC) / Consumer Price Index
reports.description: Monthly consumer price index measuring changes in the prices of a representative basket of goods and services. Produced by the central bank (distinct from the pure INE model in some neighbouring countries).
reports._notes: Flagship price statistic. Produced by the BCP rather than INE. Direct input into monetary-policy analysis and into the updating of poverty lines.

reports.title: Cuentas Nacionales / National Accounts of Paraguay
reports.description: System of national accounts producing GDP by production, expenditure and income. Quarterly and annual releases.
reports._notes: Core macroeconomic statistical system. BCP plays the central role in compilation and dissemination.

reports.title: Informe de Política Monetaria (IPoM)
reports.description: Periodic Monetary Policy Report of the central bank. Explains recent inflation, the outlook, and the implications for the policy rate under the inflation-targeting regime.
reports._notes: Flagship policy communication product. Complements higher-frequency monetary-policy decisions.

reports.title: Censo Nacional de Población y Viviendas / Population and Housing Census
reports.description: Decennial population and housing census. Provides the demographic baseline, sampling frames for household surveys, and the basis for updated population projections.
reports._notes: Foundational demographic product (2022 census). Continuously cited by EPHC design, poverty analysis and the 2025 population-projection revision.

reports.title: Índice de Pobreza Multidimensional (IPM)
reports.description: Official multidimensional poverty index capturing deprivations across multiple dimensions beyond income. Complements the monetary-poverty series.
reports._notes: Complementary structural poverty measure. Published annually for several consecutive years; series updated with the new population projections from the 2022 census.

reports.title: Balanza de Pagos / Balance of Payments
reports.description: Quarterly and annual balance of payments covering the current account, capital/financial account and changes in reserve assets.
reports._notes: Core external-accounts product. Current-account outcomes swing with commodity cycles and energy exports; goods trade is typically strong when soy and beef perform well.

reports.title: Reporte de Comercio Exterior / Merchandise Trade
reports.description: Monthly and annual statistics of exports and imports of goods, including registered trade, re-exports and other flows. Key traditional exports: soy and derivatives, beef, electricity, maize.
reports._notes: Primary high-frequency trade product. 2025 total exports ~USD 16.7 bn. Soy, beef, maize and electricity dominate; re-exports and maquila are material secondary flows.

reports.title: Tasa de Política Monetaria (TPM) / Policy interest rate
reports.description: Main monetary-policy instrument of the BCP under the inflation-targeting regime.
reports._notes: Operational policy rate. Recent levels around 5.5%. Adjusted to steer inflation toward the target band.

reports.title: Reservas Internacionales / International reserves
reports.description: Stock of international reserve assets managed by the central bank. Published at high frequency and analysed in the BOP and monetary reports.
reports._notes: Key external-buffer indicator. Continuously monitored alongside the net international investment position.

reports.title: Marco de metas de inflación — BCP
reports.description: Operational monetary-policy framework: explicit inflation targeting. The BCP sets a target (historically 4%, more recently centred near 3.5%) with a ±2 pp tolerance band and uses the TPM as the primary instrument.
reports._notes: Core policy-framework node. Continuously cited as the reference against which inflation outcomes and policy actions are evaluated.
_referenced_by: IPC and inflation analysis that refers to the target band
Market and academic commentary on Paraguayan monetary policy

reports.title: Soja y derivados — producción y exportaciones
reports.description: Statistics of soybean and soybean-product production and exports. Single most important merchandise export and the backbone of the agricultural economy.
reports._notes: Structural export leader. Often 30–40%+ of registered export value in strong years. Continuously cited in trade, BOP and rural-economy analysis.

reports.title: Carne bovina — producción y exportaciones
reports.description: Statistics of beef production and exports. Major traditional agro-export alongside soy.
reports._notes: Signature traditional export. Paraguay is a significant regional and global beef exporter; volumes and values are high-frequency trade indicators.

reports.title: Exportaciones de energía eléctrica (Itaipú / Yacyretá)
reports.description: Statistics of electricity exports from the binational hydroelectric plants (Itaipú with Brazil, Yacyretá with Argentina). Unique and material component of Paraguay’s external accounts.
reports._notes: Distinctive structural feature of the Paraguayan economy. Electricity sales to Brazil (and to a lesser extent Argentina) are a recurring and large line in the trade and current-account statistics.

reports.title: Itaipú Binacional — institutional and statistical identity
reports.description: Binational hydroelectric entity shared with Brazil. Generates the bulk of Paraguay’s electricity export revenue and is a foundational infrastructure and fiscal-revenue node.
reports._notes: Foundational binational instrument. Continuously cited in energy, trade and public-finance analysis; the treaty and compensation arrangements are recurring reference points.

reports.title: Asunción — capital statistical identity
reports.description: Capital city and primary urban economy. Core domain for EPHC labour, income and poverty analysis. Lowest departmental poverty incidence.
reports._notes: Dominant metro node. Continuously published as a distinct geographic domain. 2025 total monetary poverty ~6.0% — the lowest among departments.

reports.title: Departamento Central — core metropolitan periphery
reports.description: Department surrounding Asunción. Intermediate-to-low poverty and the largest absolute urban population mass outside the capital.
reports._notes: Completes the greater Asunción statistical geography. 2025 poverty ~9.9% — among the lowest.

reports.title: Departamento de Concepción — highest-poverty contrast
reports.description: Northern department with among the highest poverty incidence in the 2024–2025 departmental results.
reports._notes: Poverty-contrast department. 2025 total poverty ~28.7%; frequently ranks at or near the top of the departmental poverty ranking.

reports.title: Departamento de San Pedro — high-poverty contrast
reports.description: Northern/interior department with elevated poverty incidence. Completes the high-poverty northern set.
reports._notes: 2025 total poverty ~24.8%. Frequently cited alongside Concepción and Caazapá among the highest-poverty departments; also features heavily in district-level poverty maps.

reports.title: Departamento de Caazapá — high-poverty contrast
reports.description: Southern-interior department with elevated poverty incidence.
reports._notes: 2025 total poverty ~25.1%. Completes the high-poverty departmental set.

reports.title: Pobreza monetaria por departamento (INE)
reports.description: Official departmental tabulations of monetary poverty. Primary source for the inter-departmental poverty gradient.
reports._notes: Key homogeneity-test product. 2025 ranking extremes: Concepción, Caazapá, San Pedro highest; Asunción and Central lowest. National total poverty fell to ~16.0%.

reports.title: MERCOSUR (ACE 18) — marco comercial
reports.description: Southern Common Market customs-union and trade framework of which Paraguay is a founding member. Core preferential-trade arrangement with Argentina, Brazil and Uruguay.
reports._notes: Foundational regional instrument. Continuously cited in Paraguayan trade and integration analysis. Brazil is the dominant bilateral partner within the bloc.
_referenced_by: Official trade reporting with MERCOSUR partners

reports.title: Acuerdo MERCOSUR–Unión Europea
reports.description: Trade agreement between MERCOSUR and the European Union. Interim trade agreement signed in Asunción in January 2026; major preferential-access instrument for Paraguayan agro-exports.
reports._notes: Landmark external agreement. Continuously cited as a major opening for beef, soy and other agro-products into the EU market. Signed in Asunción.

reports.title: Presupuesto General de la Nación / National Budget
reports.description: Annual national budget law and subsequent execution reports covering revenues and expenditure of the central government.
reports._notes: Operational fiscal framework. Links tax and other revenues (including energy royalties) with functional spending on education, health, social protection and investment.

reports.title: Gasto público en educación y salud
reports.publisher: Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas / MEC / MSPyBS
reports.description: Public expenditure on education and health as reflected in the national budget and related functional statistics. Complements household-survey education and health modules.
reports._notes: Education and health are major functional allocations (education often the largest single share of the budget). Continuously tracked in budget execution and social-policy analysis; health coverage gaps remain a recurring policy issue.

reports.title: Royalties y compensación por cesión de energía (Itaipú)
reports.description: Fiscal transfers from Itaipú to the Paraguayan state under the Treaty Annex C: royalties and compensation for energy ceded to Brazil. Major non-tax revenue stream distributed to the central government, departments and municipalities.
reports._notes: Structural fiscal node unique to Paraguay. Hundreds of millions of USD annually (e.g. ~USD 400–500 mn range in recent full years). Part funds the national budget; part is transferred to subnational governments and social funds (e.g. FONAE for school feeding).

reports.title: Deuda pública / Public debt statistics
reports.description: Stock and flow statistics of central-government and public-sector debt (external and domestic). Key sustainability indicator.
reports._notes: Critical fiscal-sustainability node. Mid-2026 stock around USD 22 bn (~34% of GDP in recent readings). Continuously monitored in macroeconomic and policy analysis.

reports.title: Subsecretaría de Estado de Tributación (SET) — tax collection
reports.description: National tax administration. Publishes tax collection by type of tax (income tax, VAT, etc.) and performance against annual targets.
reports._notes: Primary non-energy revenue-side fiscal statistic. Complements customs revenue and the energy royalty stream.

reports.title: Ingresos fiscales del Estado / Consolidated fiscal revenues
reports.description: Consolidated view of central-government revenues including tax, customs, energy royalties/compensation and other non-tax income.
reports._notes: Operational revenue dashboard. Links the real-side economy (taxes, trade) and the binational energy complex to the financing of the national budget.

reports.title: Ley 60/90 — Régimen de promoción de inversiones
reports.description: General investment-promotion law granting tax and customs benefits for declared investment projects (capital-goods import exemptions, etc.).
reports._notes: Core horizontal investment-incentive framework. Continuously cited alongside the maquila regime as a reason firms locate in Paraguay.

reports.title: REDIEX — Red de Inversiones y Exportaciones
reports.description: National investment and export promotion network/agency. Publishes investor guides, sector profiles and trade intelligence.
reports._notes: Institutional interface between the incentive regimes (maquila, Law 60/90, free zones) and private investors and exporters.

reports.title: Departamento de Alto Paraná — industrial & border hub
reports.description: Eastern border department containing Ciudad del Este. Major commercial, industrial and re-export hub; intermediate poverty relative to the northern departments.
reports._notes: Completes the economic-geography set. Hosts significant maquila and commercial activity; poverty lower than the northern interior but higher than Asunción/Central.

reports.title: Instituto de Previsión Social (IPS) — social-security coverage
reports.description: Main social-security institution covering pensions, health insurance and other benefits for formal workers. Major formal-employment and social-protection actor.
reports._notes: Central formal-employment and social-protection node. Cotizante counts and benefit statistics complement the EPHC labour series; health coverage remains a major policy issue (large share of population without formal insurance).

reports.title: Fondo Nacional de Alimentación Escolar (FONAE)
reports.description: National school-feeding fund financed in part by Itaipú energy-compensation transfers. Links the energy-fiscal stream to a core social programme.
reports._notes: Illustrative social-programme node. Receives a large share of the Itaipú compensation-for-energy-cession resources under the current distribution law.

reports.title: Ministerio de Educación y Ciencias (MEC) — education statistics and budget
reports.description: Ministry responsible for the formal education system. Publishes enrolment, attendance and institutional statistics; major functional allocation in the national budget (constitutionally prioritised).
reports._notes: Core education node. Budget share is large (often the single largest functional category). Attendance rates from EPHC are high in primary ages but fall in the upper secondary range (~87% for 15–17). Rural–urban gaps persist.

reports.title: Tasa de asistencia escolar (EPHC)
reports.description: School-attendance rates for the school-age population derived from the continuous household survey. Key education-outcome indicator complementary to administrative enrolment data.
reports._notes: High overall attendance (~95% for 5–17) but clear age and rural–urban gradients. Complements the MEC administrative series and links education outcomes to the household-survey system.

reports.title: Cobertura de seguro médico / Health-insurance coverage
reports.description: Share of the population with formal health insurance (IPS or private). Complementary indicator to public-health service statistics.
reports._notes: Structural coverage gap. Roughly 70% of the population lacks formal insurance and depends on the public system; rural coverage is substantially lower than urban. Recurring policy and inequality theme.

reports.title: Cuentas de Salud / National Health Accounts
reports.description: Satellite accounts of health expenditure (public and private) relative to GDP and total current health spending.
reports._notes: Links the health system to the macroeconomic accounts. Public health spending has risen but remains below regional and OPS benchmarks; private out-of-pocket spending is material.

reports.title: Departamento de Itapúa — southern agricultural hub
reports.description: Southern department with significant agricultural production and intermediate-to-higher poverty relative to the capital region.
reports._notes: Completes the departmental set. Frequently appears in both poverty rankings and agricultural-production geography.

reports.title: Departamento de Caaguazú — central interior
reports.description: Central-interior department with elevated poverty incidence and significant rural population.
reports._notes: High-poverty interior department. Completes the set of departments that test the statistical hierarchy under elevated deprivation.

reports.title: ACE 35 MERCOSUR–Chile / Acuerdo Comercial Chile–Paraguay
reports.description: Economic complementarity agreement and the modernised bilateral Chile–Paraguay commercial agreement (in force 2024). Preferential access and updated disciplines on services, digital trade, SPS, TBT, etc.
reports._notes: Important Pacific-facing instrument. The 2024 bilateral modernisation deepens the older ACE 35 relationship with contemporary disciplines.
_referenced_by: MIC trade-agreement pages and origin-certificate guidance
Export strategy for the Chilean market

reports.title: Red ALADI / Acuerdos de Complementación Económica
reports.description: Network of ALADI economic-complementarity agreements (ACE) that underpin preferential trade with Chile, Bolivia, Mexico, Peru, Colombia and other partners beyond the core MERCOSUR quartet.
reports._notes: Broader Latin American preferential architecture. Continuously cited as the legal base for preferential access outside the four MERCOSUR members.

reports.title: Coeficiente de Gini / Income inequality
reports.description: Official Gini coefficient of income inequality calculated from EPHC income data. Companion indicator to the monetary-poverty series.
reports._notes: Structural inequality measure. Complements the poverty headcount and is published alongside the annual poverty results.

reports.title: Ley 7548/2025 — Nuevo régimen de incentivos fiscales para la inversión
reports.description: Updated general investment-promotion law (successor to Law 60/90). Grants tax and customs benefits for declared national and foreign investment projects.
reports._notes: Core horizontal investment-incentive framework. Replaced Law 60/90 in September 2025. Continuously cited alongside the maquila regime as a primary reason firms locate in Paraguay. (Supersedes the earlier py-ley-60-90 node conceptually; keep both for lineage if needed.)
_referenced_by: Project-approval documentation under the new regime

reports.title: Acuerdos de Promoción y Protección de Inversiones (APPI / BITs)
reports.description: Network of bilateral investment treaties (25+ countries). Provides legal protection and, in some cases, national-treatment guarantees for foreign investors.
reports._notes: Core legal infrastructure for FDI. Counterparties include Germany, Spain, France, UK, USA, Chile, Korea, Taiwan, UAE and others, plus the MERCOSUR investment framework.
_referenced_by: US State Department and other investment-climate statements

reports.title: Política Automotriz / ACE 13 sector automotor
reports.description: Automotive-sector policy and the bilateral ACE 13 regime with Argentina governing preferential trade in vehicles and auto parts, including regional-content rules and quotas.
reports._notes: Sector-specific industrial and trade instrument. ACE 13 with Argentina remains the operational preferential framework for vehicles and auto parts; Law 4838/12 provides domestic tax benefits for automotive investment.
_referenced_by: MIC origin-certification guidance for auto parts

reports.title: Consejo Nacional de Industrias Maquiladoras de Exportación (CNIME)
reports.description: Governing body of the maquila regime. Approves programmes, monitors operations and publishes sector statistics.
reports._notes: Institutional parent of the maquila system. Continuously cited in maquila export, employment and programme-approval statistics (~35k direct jobs; exports in the USD 1+ bn range).

reports.title: Consejo Nacional de Zonas Francas (CNZF)
reports.description: Governing body of the free-zone regime under Law 523/95. Supervises concessions and the special tax/customs treatment (0.5% single tax on third-country exports).
reports._notes: Institutional parent of the free-zone system. Complements the maquila regime; large-scale projects (e.g. pulp/industrial) have used free-zone concessions.

reports.title: Acuerdo de Cooperación Económica Paraguay–Taiwán
reports.description: Bilateral economic-cooperation and preferential-trade instrument with Taiwan. Includes agricultural, technological and investment-promotion elements.
reports._notes: Distinctive bilateral instrument outside the MERCOSUR external agenda. Continuously listed in official trade-agreement inventories.

reports.title: Acuerdo de Libre Comercio MERCOSUR–Israel
reports.description: Free-trade agreement between MERCOSUR and Israel providing preferential access for a large share of bilateral trade.
reports._notes: Extra-regional preferential instrument. Complements the broader MERCOSUR external agenda (EU, EFTA, Singapore, etc.).

reports.title: Acuerdo de Libre Comercio MERCOSUR–Egipto
reports.description: Free-trade agreement between MERCOSUR and Egypt providing preferential access, particularly relevant for agro-industrial exports.
reports._notes: Extra-regional preferential instrument opening an African market for Paraguayan agro-industrial products.

reports.title: Inversión Extranjera Directa / FDI statistics
reports.description: Statistics of foreign direct investment flows and stocks by sector and country of origin. Published as part of the external accounts and specialised BCP studies.
reports._notes: Core FDI statistical product. Cumulative net inflows on the order of USD 10 bn over 2008–2024; recent flows concentrated in non-financial services (commerce, telecoms, transport, real estate) alongside manufacturing and agro-industry.

reports.title: Ley 5542/2015 — Invariabilidad de la tasa impositiva
reports.description: Law allowing tax-rate invariability (stability) for up to 20 years for qualifying investment projects. Complements the general investment-incentive regime.
reports._notes: Stability instrument that reduces fiscal-policy risk for long-horizon investments. Continuously cited alongside Law 7548/2025 and the maquila/free-zone regimes.

Merchandise trade flows are a primary input into the goods account of the balance of payments.
The policy rate is the primary instrument used to steer inflation toward the target.
The Monetary Policy Report analyses outcomes against the inflation target.
Itaipú is the principal source of the electricity export statistics.
Concepción’s high poverty ranking is derived from the departmental poverty tabulations.
MERCOSUR preferential trade is a recurring analytical dimension of merchandise-trade reporting.
The EU agreement underpins preferential access for major agro-exports.
Royalties and compensation flows originate from the Itaipú binational entity under the Treaty Annex C.
FONAE is a primary destination of Itaipú compensation-for-energy-cession resources.
REDIEX promotes and explains the Law 60/90 incentive regime to investors.
School-attendance rates are derived from the continuous household survey.
IPS affiliation is a primary component of formal health-insurance coverage.
The Chile agreement underpins preferential access and origin rules for bilateral trade.
The ALADI/ACE network structures preferential access to multiple Latin American partners.
The Gini coefficient is computed from the same income distribution underlying the poverty estimates.
Itapúa’s poverty ranking is derived from the departmental poverty tabulations.
Caaguazú’s elevated poverty ranking is derived from the departmental poverty tabulations.
REDIEX promotes and channels applications under the updated investment-incentive regime.
The BIT network is a core legal foundation cited in investment-promotion materials.
ACE 13 and the automotive policy structure preferential trade and origin rules for vehicles and auto parts.
The Taiwan agreement underpins preferential bilateral trade and cooperation.
The Israel FTA expands preferential extra-regional market access.
